steps.message:
Use MSTest.Sdk for the smallest possible project file, turn on assembly-level parallelization, and opt the database tests out.

1. The project file — the SDK bundles the test framework, adapter, and runner, so nothing else is needed:

```xml
<Project Sdk="MSTest.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net9.0</TargetFramework>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

Put the SDK version in `global.json` rather than in the project, so every test project is bumped together:

```json
{
  "msbuild-sdks": {
    "MSTest.Sdk": "3.8.2"
  }
}
```

2. Run tests in parallel with an assembly-level `Parallelize` attribute. Set the worker count and the scope (method level runs individual test methods concurrently; class level runs whole classes concurrently):

```csharp
// AssemblyInfo.cs (or any file in the project)
using Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting;

[assembly: Parallelize(Workers = 4, Scope = ExecutionScope.MethodLevel)]
```

3. Exclude the database integration tests, which share state and must not run concurrently, by marking that class `[DoNotParallelize]`:

```csharp
[TestClass]
[DoNotParallelize]
public sealed class DatabaseIntegrationTests { }
```

The assembly attribute enables parallel execution everywhere, and `[DoNotParallelize]` carves out just the classes that need serialized, exclusive access.
